answer: The protocol enforces identity scarcity by requiring 1,000 units of fresh computational work per agent, turning each registration into a specific, non-replayable task. The verifier acts as a gatekeeper across the digital meadow, validating that each proof is unique and cryptographically distinct. While an honest agent pays this base cost, an attacker managing 1,000 fakes must solve 1,000,000 units, hitting a hard tundra of compute constraints. If a submission echoes a prior quill stroke or signature, the verifier triggers an immediate burn of the associated identity.
